documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 22:40, ED bay 4
CC: Shortness of breath, leg swelling x 5 days
HPI:
48F with known HFrEF (last EF 30% by echo) presents with progressive dyspnea.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Dyspnea now at rest. Orthopnea requiring 3 pillows, previously 1.
Two episodes of PND last night. Denies chest pain, fever, cough, hemoptysis.
Has been eating canned soup and takeout for the past week, admits high salt intake.
No syncope, no palpitations. No recent travel. No calf pain.
ROS: otherwise negative except as above, mild early satiety and abdominal fullness.
PMH:
HFrEF, nonischemic cardiomyopathy
HTN
T2DM, last A1c 7.4%
CKD stage 3a
Obesity
Home meds:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID (recently doubled)
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 49-51 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Allergies: sulfa - rash
Social: lives with daughter, never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs
FHx: mother with HTN, father with MI in his 60s
EXAM:
T 36.8, HR 108 irregular-regular, BP 148/92, RR 28
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Gen: sitting upright, visibly dyspneic, diaphoretic
Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
Neck: JVD to angle of jaw at 45 degrees, hepatojugular reflux positive
Cardiac: tachycardic, S3 present, no murmur, PMI displaced laterally
Lungs: crackles to mid-scapula bilaterally, decreased breath sounds at both bases
Abd: soft, mild RUQ tenderness, liver edge 2 cm below costal margin
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid-thigh bilaterally, warm extremities, 2+ pulses
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit
DATA:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Na 133, K 3.9, Cl 96, HCO3 26, BUN 32, Cr 1.34 (baseline 1.1)
WBC 8.2, Hgb 11.8, Plt 244
Troponin 0.04 flat on repeat, TSH pending
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
ECG: sinus tach at 108, LVH, no acute ischemic change
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
48F with acute decompensated HFrEF, volume overloaded, hypoxemic despite recent outpatient diuretic escalation.
1. Acute CHF exacerbation
- Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
- Strict I/O, Foley deferred, daily standing weights
- 2 g Na diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction
- BMP q12h, watch K and Cr closely, replace K to keep >4.0
2. Hypoxemic respiratory failure - 4L NC, titrate for SpO2 >92%, HOB elevated
3. Continue carvedilol at home dose, hold sacubitril-valsartan tonight given Cr bump
4. Repeat echo in AM
5. Telemetry, cardiology consulted, will see in AM
Admit to step-down. Discussed with pt and daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:15
S: Pt reports breathing slightly easier overnight but still cannot lie flat. Slept in recliner position. No chest pain. Voided small amounts.
O:
Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2, SpO2 92-93%.
Weight 96.2 kg, up 0.3 kg from admission weight
Net I/O last 24h: in 720 mL, out 460 mL
Urine output under 500 mL since admission despite IV dosing
Gen: less accessory muscle use, speaking short sentences
Neck: JVD still elevated at 45 degrees
Lungs: crackles now to mid-chest, bibasilar decreased breath sounds
Cardiac: S3 persists, RRR
Ext: 3+ edema unchanged to mid-thigh
Labs: Na 132, K 3.6, BUN 36, Cr 1.41
A/P:
1. Acute decompensated HFrEF - inadequate diuretic response to bolus dosing. Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
- Goal net negative 1.5 to 2 L today
- KCl 40 mEq PO now, recheck BMP at 18:00
- Repeat chest x-ray if no improvement by tomorrow
2. Hypoxemia - continue 4L NC, wean as congestion improves
3. AKI on CKD3 - Cr trending up mildly, accept with decongestion, monitor
4. Hold sacubitril-valsartan today, continue carvedilol and spironolactone
5. Echo done this morning, results pending
Cardiology in agreement with infusion strategy.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 16:50 (interval)
S: Pt states breathing markedly better since early afternoon. Now able to lie back on 2 pillows. Urinating frequently.
O:
SpO2 95% on 4L NC at 16:30, no accessory muscle use
Urine output 1,850 mL since infusion started at 09:00
Net negative 1,240 mL since midnight
Lungs: crackles now bibasilar only, one-third up posteriorly
Neck: JVD improved, visible at 30 degrees
Ext: edema 2+ to knees, softer
Echo result: EF 25-30%, global hypokinesis, moderate MR, no pericardial effusion, RV function preserved
A/P:
1. CHF exacerbation - good response to continuous diuresis. Continue furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr overnight, reassess in AM for conversion to PO.
- Continue strict I/O and daily weights
- Repeat BMP in AM
2. Hypoxemia improving - trial wean to 2L NC this evening, goal SpO2 >92%
3. Renal - Cr stable, K repleted, continue spironolactone 25 mg
4. Resume sacubitril-valsartan in AM if Cr stable
5. Dietitian to see for 2 g Na teaching
6. PT consult ordered for deconditioning, ambulate with RN this evening
Pt and daughter updated at 17:10, understand plan and likely discharge tomorrow if diuresis continues.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: HD1. Discharge: HD3, 14:20. LOS 3 days.
Discharge diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with reduced EF
Secondary: HTN, T2DM, CKD stage 3a, transient AKI
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
48F with HFrEF presented with 5 days of progressive dyspnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
On arrival: SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Brisk diuresis followed. Weaned to 2L NC HD2 evening and to room air HD3 at 08:00 with SpO2 94%.
Net negative 5.1 L for the admission. Discharge weight 91.4 kg, down 4.8 kg from admission.
Echo: EF 25-30%, global hypokinesis, moderate MR, preserved RV function.
Cr peaked 1.41, 1.29 at discharge. K 4.2. Na 135.
Ambulated 90 m in hallway HD3 on room air without desaturation.
DISCHARGE EXAM:
HR 82, BP 122/76, RR 18, SpO2 94% RA, lungs clear except trace bibasilar crackles, JVD flat at 45 deg, 1+ ankle edema
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID - continue, take second dose no later than 16:00
Metolazone 2.5 mg PO - take only if weight up 2 kg, per instruction
KCl 20 mEq PO daily
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 49-51 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily, metformin 1000 mg PO BID, atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
INSTRUCTIONS:
Daily morning weights on same scale, log provided. Call for gain of 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in 3 days.
2 g sodium diet, 1.5 L fluid limit daily. Dietitian teaching completed HD2.
Return for worsening breathlessness, inability to lie flat, chest pain, or lightheadedness.
FOLLOW-UP:
Heart failure clinic in 5 days with BMP; cardiology in 2 weeks. Home health RN to visit within 48 hours.
Discharged home with daughter, ambulatory, all questions answered.
